newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers agrees two-year Namibia wage deal.
newsitem.headline: De Beers agrees two-year Namibia wage deal.

text.p: De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd said on Monday that Namdeb Diamond Corp had agreed a two-year wage deal with the Mineworkers Union of Namibia (MUN).
The two-year agreement was the first of its kind and both sides said it augured well for increased cooperation.
The wage discussions, which started on June 3, were concluded on June 18 -- the faster conclusion in the company's history.

Under the deal, unskilled and semi-skilled workers will receive wage increases of 9.9 percent plus a 1.1 percent annualised service award. Skilled workers will receive 9.5 percent plus individual awards of 1.5 percent.
Effective June 1998, employees in the bargaining unit will receive increases of nine percent plus not less than two percent in the form of merit.
De Beers and the Namibian government are equal partners in Namdeb.
